idiom_name: striped lock array keyed by a hash (key -> bounded lock set)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: pick a stripe count N from the desired concurrency (a small multiple of the core count, or a power of two so the modulo becomes a mask), allocate N locks once, and map every key through a stable hash reduced modulo N. Acquire the key's stripe before any compound operation on that key's state and release it afterwards; because equal keys always map to the same stripe, per-key invariants survive. For operations covering several keys, collect the distinct stripe indices, sort them and acquire in ascending order (or use the platform's ordered bulk acquisition), releasing in reverse order. Keep the stripe array private and the hash independent of mutable key state; pad or separately allocate stripes when they would otherwise share cache lines. When the guarded state is a plain map, prefer an existing concurrent container instead.
pitfalls: Collisions are expected: never assume that two distinct keys can be held at the same time, and de-duplicate stripe indices before locking several keys.
The stripe count and hash must be documented and stable for the structure's lifetime; an unstable hash silently breaks per-key mutual exclusion.
Fixed stripe counts do not resize: plan the concurrency target up front or rebuild the structure on reconfiguration.

Wrong move: assume distinct keys map to distinct stripes -> collisions serialize work and can deadlock multi-key callers that acquire in inconsistent orders -> instead treat collisions as expected, deduplicate stripe indices and use a global acquisition order (for example bulkGet).

Wrong move: mutate a key or its hash-relevant state while it is stored -> later operations can select a different stripe and violate per-key exclusion -> instead require immutable keys or a hash stable for the structure's lifetime.

Wrong move: hold a stripe across slow I/O or unbounded callbacks -> unrelated keys sharing that stripe inherit the latency and throughput collapses -> instead keep the critical section bounded and perform external work after releasing the stripe.
